summary: Shallow embedding pilot of Cooper's TTR (2023, Appendix A) that maps TTR directly onto Coq's native type system: ptypes as Prop-valued predicates (propositions-as-types), record types (A11) as dependent Coq Records (ManRuns, DogChasesCat, JohnRuns with a manifest field as an equality), witnesses as inhabitants, singleton types (A6) as sig-equality types, join/meet as sum/product, function types (A4) as Coq arrows, subtyping via a declared projection Coercion, and Luo-style generalized quantifiers. The second half is a structured feasibility essay in comments: five documented breakages of the shallow approach (types not first-class values; no reasoning about model-relative empty types; no merge of record types A11.3; no relabelling A1; no model-indexed modal systems A9) plus a two-way TTR-vs-MTT comparison (dot-types for copredication demoed via a PhyInfo record; coercive subtyping; CNs-as-types; universe hierarchy vs A10). One trivial demo theorem (john_runs_proof, modus ponens under section hypotheses). The file's stated conclusion: the features Cooper's dialogue theory needs are exactly the ones the shallow embedding cannot provide, motivating the companion deep embedding (TTR_base/types/records).

sources.citation: Cooper, R. (2023). From Perception to Communication: An Enriched Approach to the Semantics and Pragmatics of Dialogue. Oxford University Press. (Appendix A: A1, A4, A6, A9, A10, A11; p. 397 quoted in header.)
Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2020). Formal Semantics in Modern Type Theories. Wiley/ISTE. (Secondary source for the MTT comparison half.)
Luo, Z. (2012). Common nouns as types. LACL 2012. (Dot-types, coercive subtyping, CNs-as-types referenced in the comparison.)

evidence: The covered fragment (ptypes, dependent record types A11, singletons A6, function types A4, witnesses-as-inhabitants) tracks Cooper's definitions closely and cites appendix items by number.

Two core definitions are changed by the file's own admission: meet as product (Cooper requires one object witnessing both types, lines 139-146) and subtyping as declared coercions rather than semantic inclusion (lines 110-119).

Cooper's headline dialogue machinery — merge A11.3, relabelling A1, model-indexed modality A9, types as first-class values — is entirely missing, and the file documents each omission explicitly as Problems 1-5 (lines 195-260).

No named source claim is proved as a theorem; the single Qed is a trivial demo. Zero propositional axioms: all 13 Parameters are signature-only (types, individual and predicate constants), rubric §3a.
simplifications: ptype witnesses (situations) become Coq proof objects with no model parameter
record types lose labelled-set structure and paths
omissions: stratification Type^n (A10, noted as free in Coq's universe hierarchy but not formalized)
additions: Luo MTT comparison block: dot-type copredication demo (PhyInfo), generalized quantifiers, coercive subtyping
extended comparative essay in comments (what each framework gives the other)

determination_rationale: The file is a deliberate feasibility probe and its own verdict is the evidence: the MLTT-like core of TTR (dependent records, ptypes, singletons, function types) lands directly on Coq, but Cooper's distinctive operations — merge, relabelling, dynamic type creation, model-indexed modality — require types to be first-class values, which the shallow embedding provably cannot supply (Problem 1: type-value universe separation, artifact class ii); recovering them means re-founding via the companion deep embedding's VType injection (per OVERVIEW_ttr_mtt.tex). Meet and subtyping had to be changed even in the covered fragment. Determination is provisional on this pilot; the deep-embedding files are the ones that could raise or confirm it.

artifact_classes.description: type-value collapse blocked: Cooper's types-as-values (frames, dynamic type creation, storing types in record fields) cannot be expressed because Coq separates Set/Type from values — documented as Problems 1 and 5 and as 'the main thing we lose going shallow'

missing native structure: no merge operation on Coq record types (A11.3), no relabelling of fields (A1), no semantic subtyping — coercions must be declared per projection; the deep embedding's VType is the workaround

notes: Record produced by the batch audit sweep of 2026-09-05; the file predates the atlas zero-axiom discipline and freely uses 13 Parameters, though all are signature-only (no propositional axioms); the anchored theorem grep returns 0 because the single trivial Theorem is section-indented.
